sections.content: How many people are "assemblers and routine operatives (other)"?

34,320 people

were counted on the census as "assemblers and routine operatives (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work perform assembly and routine operative tasks not elsewhere classified.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "assemblers and routine operatives (other)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "assemblers and routine operatives (other)", 12% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "assemblers and routine operatives (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "assemblers and routine operatives (other)" included:

  • records clerks and assistants
  • other administrative occupations
  • science, engineering and production technicians (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "assemblers and routine operatives (other)" there were more men than women (63% compared with 37%).

This means "assemblers and routine operatives (other)" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 63% and women made up 37% of "assemblers and routine operatives (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "assemblers and routine operatives (other)" included:

  • business sales executives
  • quality control and planning engineers
  • textile process operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "assemblers and routine operatives (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "assemblers and routine operatives (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "assemblers and routine operatives (other)", 9.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.7% compared with 13.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.5%) than self-employed (4.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the West Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the same region of the West Midlands.
